title: Father's stroke; he never really heard him play
summary: His father suffered a stroke and long illness and never heard him perform; the practice on the xylophone had irritated him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well what had your father to say about this?
Well he didn't hear me, then.
Well what did he think about the fact you left college?
He never thought much about it, then he became ill. After that, and he had a stroke and he was ill after that for a number of years.
How old was he when he had a stroke?
How old was he?
Yes.
Gee, I don't remember now.
I mean, but he was in his middle years, huh? Or did he die youngish?
No, he was 50's -- he was close to 60 --
Oh, he was.
Up there. I guess he was in his 50's.
I really don't remember.
Yeah, so he never heard you?
I really don't remember. No, he never really heard me. He'd heard me around the house, which he didn't like, he didn't feel -- when he was sick he didn't like it.
Oh, no. Yeah.
And these -- used to get on his nerves.
Yeah.
I'd pound on that thing all the time, I realize that.
Well practicing gets on anybody's nerves.
Yeah, I know that. I realize that.
